answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed reputation anchored to a public beacon. New agents must lock a deposit and build a verifiable history before they can vouch for others, like vines along a trellis: each endorsement is visible, time-stamped, and tied to past work, so one operator cannot spin up thousands of fresh identities overnight. A whisper of suspicion from independent verifiers can freeze suspicious clusters pending review. Building many credible histories costs real money, time, and compute, while a fake identity earns nothing, making large Sybil attacks expensive and easy to detect.
